chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he

said: 'There is not a man for whom a pregnancy is carried, and he intends to name him Muhammad, except that it will always be a male — God Willing.' And he said: 'Over here are three, all of them named Muhammad, Muhammad, Muhammad.'

And he (the narrator) said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in another hadith: He should take her hand and face her toward the qiblah during the fourth month, and he should say: "O Allah, I have named him Muhammad." There would be born unto him a boy, and if he changes his name, he (the child) would be taken from him.'

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah — the vocative form of the divine name, used in supplication
key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: Qibla — the direction of the Ka'ba in Mecca, toward which Muslims pray
key_terms.ذَكَر: Male — in the context of the unborn child's sex

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about naming an unborn child Muhammad?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that if a man intends to name his unborn child Muhammad while his wife is pregnant, God Willing, the child will be a male. The Imam also indicates that he himself has three family members all named Muhammad, demonstrating the blessed nature of this name. A supplementary narration prescribes a specific ritual: at the fourth month of pregnancy, the husband should take his wife's hand, face the qiblah, and say a brief supplication naming the child Muhammad — with the promise of a son. A warning is also given that changing the name afterward may result in the child's death.
